_comment:
The catalog of every runtime-tunable knob in the fleet. This file is the SCHEMA (name, type, range, default, meaning); settings.json next to config.json holds only the values someone changed. Splitting them that way means a default improved in a release reaches every install, instead of being frozen the first time anyone saved a value.

This is deliberately NOT config.json. config.json is wiring — addresses, tokens, which backend, which camera — the things that make the fleet exist, and getting them wrong takes it offline. These are behaviour knobs: how long to wait, how loud is loud, how many items fit. They are safe to change while a customer is standing there, so the agent is allowed to change them itself.

scope decides who has to be told about a change:
  server  - mcp-core reads it live on the next use. Nothing to push.
  box     - pushed to every ESP32-S3-BOX over its reverse channel (or HTTP), stored in the box's NVS, applied on the next listen/session.
  device  - pushed to spc devices (the OrangePi) via PATCH /settings.
  agent   - not used by mcp-core at all; served to the agent webhook, which fetches it. Kept here so a restaurant's rules live in the same place as everything else.

`restart` marks a knob that only takes effect on the next mcp-core start (a timer armed once at boot). It still saves and still reports honestly rather than pretending to have applied.

settings.summary: How long the box must hear silence, after real speech, before it stops recording on its own.
settings.guidance: This is the auto-stop knob. Lower feels snappy but clips people who pause mid-sentence to think; higher is patient but leaves an awkward gap before the reply. Raise it for customers who speak slowly or in a second language; lower it for a fast queue.

settings.summary: Peak int16 sample level below which a 32ms chunk counts as quiet.
settings.guidance: The room's noise floor, measured. If auto-stop never fires, the background is louder than this — raise it. If the box cuts people off mid-word, it is treating speech as silence — lower it. On-site measurement on this hardware at mic_gain_db=30: median ambient ~646, p90 ~1360, spikes ~3800. Re-measure after changing listen.mic_gain_db, since the two move together.

settings.summary: Consecutive loud chunks needed before the box believes speech actually started.
settings.guidance: Stops a single click, door slam or chair scrape from arming the silence timer and ending the turn instantly. Raise it in a noisy room; 1 makes the box hair-trigger.

settings.summary: Hard cap on a single listen turn, whatever the voice activity detector thinks.
settings.guidance: The safety net for a box left recording in an empty room. The maximum is 20 because the recording buffer is allocated once at boot for 20 seconds of 16kHz mono; asking for more would need a reflash, not a setting.

settings.summary: Microphone input gain, applied at the start of every recording.
settings.guidance: Raise it when customers stand back from the box and come through faint; lower it when close talkers clip and transcription turns to mush. Changing this invalidates listen.silence_peak — the noise floor scales with it.

settings.summary: How long with no sign of the customer before the box declares the session over and the order resets.
settings.guidance: Measured caution: the presence radar reports motion, not stillness, so someone standing quietly reads as absent for 10s+ at a time. Below ~20s this ends sessions with the customer still standing there, and their next small movement starts a fresh one and re-greets them. The timer is fed by taps and speech as well as radar.

settings.summary: How long a status badge (SENT, ERROR) stays on the box screen.
settings.guidance: Purely cosmetic pacing. Long enough to read, short enough not to hide the reply behind it.

settings.summary: How long the help QR screen stays up after a double tap of RST before the box returns to normal.
settings.guidance: Long enough for someone to fetch a phone and scan; short enough that a box left on the help screen recovers itself.

settings.summary: How long the counter camera watches for a payment QR before giving up on the pay flow.
settings.guidance: Long enough to fish a phone out of a pocket, short enough that a customer who walks off does not hold the box hostage.

settings.summary: Gap between camera frames while watching for a payment QR.
settings.guidance: Each frame is a capture plus a decode, so this is a CPU-vs-latency trade. Below ~750ms the scans start overlapping on a slow machine and buy nothing.

settings.summary: How long the PAID confirmation stays on screen before the box resets for the next customer.
settings.guidance: The customer needs to see that it worked. Too short reads as if the payment was ignored.

settings.summary: Turns of conversation kept for the local_llm backend before the oldest are dropped.
settings.guidance: Only affects the plain local-LLM path; a webhook agent keeps its own session state and ignores this. Raising it grows every prompt and slows replies on a small local model.

settings.summary: What the box says when a customer first walks up. Empty falls back to greeting_text in config.json.
settings.guidance: Spoken once and cached as audio, so a change costs one synthesis and then nothing. Keep it to a sentence — it plays before the customer has decided to engage.

settings.summary: Language hint sent to the STT engine. Empty falls back to speech.stt.language in config.json; "auto" lets the engine detect; a code (e.g. "en", "zh", "ms") biases toward one language.
settings.guidance: Automatic language detection is unreliable on short, noisy kiosk utterances — switch this when a box gets a run of customers ordering in one language (part of the Manglish/BM handling). Applies to the very next transcription, no restart needed.

settings.summary: How often mcp-core re-tells every known box where this server is.
settings.guidance: The cure for a box stuck on NO SERVER after the server's IP moved. Shorter recovers faster after a DHCP change and costs one tiny HTTP request per box per round.

settings.summary: How long an mDNS-announced box stays on the adoptable list after its last announcement.
settings.guidance: A box that is unplugged never says goodbye, so this is what eventually removes it. Long enough to survive a couple of missed multicast rounds.

settings.summary: How often to re-ask the network which boxes are out there.
settings.guidance: Only a backstop — boxes announce themselves when they boot. Worth shortening on a network that drops multicast, which is most managed WiFi.

settings.summary: Window over which failed reverse-channel authentications are counted per source IP.
settings.guidance: Brute-force throttling for the one endpoint that may be exposed publicly. A real box authenticates once and never fails, so this should never affect the fleet.

settings.summary: Failed authentications from one IP within the window before it is throttled.
settings.guidance: Behind a relay every client shares one bucket, so this is deliberately a global-ish cap rather than a per-client one.

settings.summary: Grace added to a Pi's listen deadline on top of the recording length it was asked for.
settings.guidance: The Pi cannot answer until it has finished recording, so its deadline is per-call. This margin covers uploading the WAV back over a slow link — raise it on a weak connection.

settings.summary: Deadline for a camera capture on a Pi, measured from mcp-core.
Deadline for a Pi to synthesize and play a sentence, measured from mcp-core.
settings.guidance: Must stay comfortably above spc.speak_timeout_s on the Pi itself, or mcp-core gives up while the Pi is still talking.

settings.summary: Deadline for a face or panel update on a Pi, measured from mcp-core.
How long the Pi itself allows a camera capture to run before killing it.
How long the Pi itself allows synthesis plus playback to run before killing it.
settings.guidance: Keep it below spc.timeout_speak_ms so the Pi is the one that gives up first and can report why.

settings.summary: How long the Pi allows a presence/sensor command to run.
How long the Pi allows a mixer volume command to run.
The Pi's own auto-stop: silence after speech before it stops recording.
settings.guidance: The OrangePi equivalent of listen.silence_hold_ms. A caller that passes silence_s explicitly overrides this; it is the default when they do not.

settings.summary: Default hard cap on one listen turn on the Pi when the caller does not give one.
Whether the order-taker must hear an explicit confirmation before finalizing.
settings.guidance: Turning this off makes a small model's premature 'confirmed' finalize a half-spoken order. It exists for kiosks where a screen tap is the only confirmation.

settings.summary: Rows the order screen shows before it stops listing them.
settings.guidance: The box's 320x240 screen fits about five rows at a readable size. Raising this past what fits does not make the rest visible.

settings.summary: How long the customer is told their food will take.
settings.guidance: The one number in the whole conversation that changes with the queue rather than with the hardware. Raise it at lunch rush.

settings.summary: Sampling temperature for the order-extraction model.
settings.guidance: This is structured extraction, not writing. At the usual ~0.8 default a small model dropped items from orders it had just been read. Leave it at 0 unless you are deliberately experimenting.

settings.summary: Currency prefix printed before every price.
settings.guidance: Display only — it does no conversion. Prices themselves live in the menu.
